groups.title: Sequence diagrams
groups.description: Follow a conversation, its branches, and the work happening in parallel.

examples.title: A request, end to end
examples.description: Actors and aliases, request and return arrows, a self-call, nested activations, notes, numbering, and explicit line breaks.

examples.title: Branches and retries
examples.description: A bounded retry loop with alternative responses, an optional step, and an early exit.

examples.title: Parallel work, one commit
examples.description: Parallel branches, asynchronous messages, and a critical region with a recovery option.

examples.title: A worker's lifetime
examples.description: Grouped participants, typed database and queue participants, a highlighted region, and a worker created and destroyed during the conversation.

groups.title: Flowcharts
groups.description: Turn decisions and dependencies into paths, shapes, and nested systems.

examples.title: From draft to publication
examples.description: Top-to-bottom decisions, a retry cycle, labeled branches, and several destinations.

examples.title: A vocabulary of shapes
examples.description: Fourteen traditional node shapes with solid, dotted, thick, open, bidirectional, circle, and cross connections.

examples.title: Inside a delivery system
examples.description: Nested subgraphs, local directions, chained and fan-out connections, and edges crossing group boundaries.

examples.title: Labels with a little emphasis
examples.description: Markdown bold and italic, wrapped labels, explicit line breaks, entities, classDef, class assignment, node and link styles, and supported shape metadata.

groups.title: State diagrams
groups.description: Describe a lifecycle, then open it up to show nested and concurrent behavior.

examples.title: An order's lifecycle
examples.description: Initial and final states, aliases, descriptions, labeled transitions, a cancellation path, and a multiline note.

examples.title: Two parts of one workflow
examples.description: A composite state containing concurrent regions, local initial and final states, and an inner direction.

examples.title: Choose, fork, and join
examples.description: A choice branches into approval or concurrent tasks, which meet at a join; classes and inline styles distinguish outcomes.

groups.title: Class diagrams
groups.description: Show the shape of a type, the relationships around it, and the modules it belongs to.

examples.title: What a class contains
examples.description: Generic types, typed attributes and methods, public/private/protected/package visibility, an interface annotation, and static and abstract members.

examples.title: How types relate
examples.description: Inheritance, realization, association, dependency, aggregation, composition, relation labels, and multiplicities.

examples.title: A small application
examples.description: Nested namespaces, cross-module relationships, attached and standalone notes, and class styling.

groups.title: Entity relationship diagrams
groups.description: Read the cardinalities first, then add the fields and boundaries of a real data model.

examples.title: One, none, or many
examples.description: Exactly one, zero or one, zero or more, and one or more; identifying and non-identifying relationships with role labels.

examples.title: Fields that tell a story
examples.description: Entity aliases, attribute types, primary/foreign/unique keys, combined keys, nullable attributes, and comments.

examples.title: A store in two domains
examples.description: Grouped entities, a left-to-right direction, cross-group relationships, attributes, and styles applied to entities and groups.
